archetype.name: Lost Season (luckier than it looks)
archetype.definition: A last-place year in which a hot April gave way to five losing months out of six, and 75 wins flattered a club whose run differential played closer to 65.

report.headline: An April mirage, then a pitching staff that couldn't hold; 75 wins flattered them.

recap.finish: 75-87, last in the NL Central, 28 games behind Milwaukee; missed the postseason
recap.body:
Cincinnati opened 2026 looking like a step forward from last year's 83-79. It went 17-9 in April. That record was already a little hollow: the Reds outscored opponents 119-118 that month, so the start came from winning close games, not from beating teams soundly. Once the close games stopped breaking their way, the team underneath showed itself. May went 10-17 and June 9-17, and by midsummer the season was effectively over. July (13-12) was the only winning month after April. The longest losing streak reached eight, and the club never won more than five in a row.

The real story is in the margin. The Reds were outscored by 160 runs over the year, a Run Diff / G of -0.99 that ranked 28th of 30. Their W vs Run Diff of +9.8 was the best in the league, meaning a team with this differential would normally finish around 65-97. That is ten wins of mostly close-game fortune propping up a record that was already last in the division. The site's 26th-of-30 ranking is closer to the truth than the 75 wins.

Run prevention was the main failure. Team ERA climbed from 3.86 in 2025 to 4.83, and the Def Rank fell from 11th to 28th. Chase Burns was the lone exception and a genuine ace: 2.86 ERA, 3.24 FIP, a 29.4% K rate and 4.3 WAR. The other four starters struck out batters only 17-18% of the time. Brady Singer (5.85 ERA) and Rhett Lowder (5.74) were hit hard over a combined 290 innings, and Nick Lodolo's 5.70 FIP says his 4.97 ERA was, if anything, kind to him. The rotation graded F. The bullpen (D) offered little relief: Brock Burke's 2.30 ERA came with a 12.7% walk rate and a 3.76 FIP, and Ron Marinaccio gave up a 6.09 ERA in 57.2 innings. The staff unraveled late, allowing 164 runs in August and 143 in September, nearly six a game across the final two months.

The offense (OPS .699, Off Rank 27th, hitters graded D) had two stars and too many holes. Elly De La Cruz was the second-ranked shortstop on the site, with 6.4 WAR, a 139 wRC+, 30 homers and 30 steals. Sal Stewart, an All-Star, played all 162 games and drove in 112 runs with 32 homers and a 112 wRC+. Behind them the lineup was mostly average bats, plus two regulars who sank it. Matt McLain posted a 67 wRC+ across 496 plate appearances. TJ Friedl managed a 43 wRC+ and -0.7 WAR in 272. Eugenio Suárez hit 26 homers but contributed just 0.4 WAR as a DH with a .307 OBP. The defense did improve: Fielding Runs of -1 is far better than the -20s of 2021-24, but it wasn't nearly enough to offset the pitching.

The Reds finished 4-6 over their last ten, including losses of 2-8 to the Dodgers and 1-9 to the Cubs. That is a fair summary of a team that couldn't keep pace with the contenders it faced.

highlights.title: De La Cruz played like a star
highlights.body: De La Cruz ranked second among 51 shortstops on the site, combining a 139 wRC+ with 30 homers, 30 steals and positive defense (4.1 Def Runs). His 6.4 WAR was more than three times any other Reds hitter. That is a full-season, all-around profile rather than a hot stretch, and he is the clearest foundation the numbers show.

highlights.title: Chase Burns was a true ace
highlights.body: Burns ranked 18th of 215 starters, with a 2.86 ERA backed by a 3.24 FIP and a 29.4% strikeout rate. The FIP close behind the ERA says his performance was earned, not lucky. He was worth 4.3 WAR. The rest of the rotation combined for less than 3.

highlights.title: Stewart's durable run production
highlights.body: Stewart played all 162 games, hit 32 homers, drove in 112 runs and made the All-Star team. His 112 wRC+ is good rather than elite, and he graded as a solid regular at first base (12th of 44). Still, few hitters on this roster gave the Reds that kind of steady volume.

lowlights.title: The rotation behind Burns collapsed
lowlights.body: Singer, Lowder, Lodolo and Abbott combined for about 565 innings with ERAs from 4.61 to 5.85 and strikeout rates stuck near 17-18%. Their FIPs (4.70-5.70) confirm the results weren't bad luck: these starters didn't miss bats and put too many runners on, with WHIPs of 1.45 or worse. Team ERA rose a full run from 2025, and the rotation graded F.

lowlights.title: Record propped up by close games
lowlights.body: A W vs Run Diff of +9.8, the league's highest, means the Reds won about ten more games than being outscored by 160 runs would normally allow. That kind of edge rarely carries over from one year to the next. The underlying team was closer to 65 wins than 75.

lowlights.title: Dead spots in the lineup
lowlights.body: McLain (67 wRC+ in 496 PA) and Friedl (43 wRC+, -0.7 WAR) gave back much of what De La Cruz and Stewart produced. Suárez's 26 homers came with a .307 OBP and 0.4 WAR. Those holes help explain an offense that ranked 27th in runs per game and graded D.

arc.note: A 17-9 April built on a near-even run differential gave way to 10-17 and 9-17 in May and June. After a .500-ish July, the pitching gave up nearly six runs a game over August and September.

recap.nextYear: What carries forward is a two-man core: De La Cruz (6.4 WAR) on offense and Burns (4.3 WAR, a 2.86 ERA backed by a 3.24 FIP) on the mound, with Stewart as a durable run producer. Nearly everything else needs work. The rotation behind Burns graded F, with four starters whose low strikeout rates and high FIPs say the results were earned. The bullpen graded D and walked too many. Second base and the outfield produced little, and Steer ended the year on the 60-day IL. The 2025 staff posted a 3.86 ERA and ranked 11th in run prevention, so these groups have performed better before, but the sheet doesn't explain the drop. The most important caution is the +9.8 W vs Run Diff: a repeat of this run differential without that close-game luck would produce a far worse record than 75-87.

confidence.note: Full 162-game season; the run differential and the pitching numbers point the same way.
